D018-D020_h001.question:
It’s been over a month now since that awful incident at school, and I just… I can’t shake it. Every night, the dreams are back. I’m right there again, seeing it all unfold, feeling that same terror. When I wake up, I just feel so drained. Honestly, getting anything done at school, even small things that used to be second nature, feels impossible. I’ve lost all my drive. I find myself just sitting there, staring at paperwork, unable to start.

I’m so angry with some of the parents, even though it’s probably not fair. I keep replaying conversations, thinking about what they did or didn’t do, feeling like they’re responsible for putting us all in that situation. And the shame… I still feel this deep, burning shame that I couldn’t protect my students better, that I failed somehow. Even picking out what to wear in the morning or deciding what to have for dinner has become an agonizing decision. My husband gets frustrated because I just freeze up. And if there’s a sudden loud noise, my heart races so hard my whole body trembles, and it takes absolutely forever for me to calm down. It’s been going on for well over a month now, much longer than I ever expected.
D018-D020_h001.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h002.question:
It's been over a month now, since... the accident at work. Every night, if I even manage to get some sleep after my shift, it's the same nightmares. I relive it all, the noise, the dust, the cries for help. I wake up in a cold sweat, my heart pounding.

My friends keep calling, asking why I haven’t been out, but I just don’t have it in me. The thought of engaging with anyone, beyond a quick "hello," feels too much. I've been cancelling plans, feeling like I can't really connect anymore. And honestly, I keep replaying it, thinking about how I could have done something, anything, to stop it. If only I had reacted faster.

I feel this constant knot of fear in my stomach, like something terrible is always about to happen again. Even small decisions, like what to eat for dinner, leave me staring blankly at the fridge for ages. And the noise! The other day, a dropped wrench made me jump so hard I nearly hit my head. This feeling... it hasn't let up since the incident. It’s been over five weeks now, and it’s just as intense as it was that first night.
D018-D020_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h003.question: “It’s been over a month now since that night, since I found that kid… and things just aren't right. I still can’t shake it. D018-D020_h005.question:

I keep replaying it in my head, seeing the car coming, feeling the impact, over and over again, even when I don't want to. It's constant.

I used to love my job, the thrill of finding someone their dream home, but now? I barely care. Nothing really excites me anymore, not even the little things my husband and I used to enjoy. D018-D020_h006.question:
"It’s been over a year now since that car accident, and honestly, things just haven’t been the same. One minute I’m talking about highlights, the next I’m replaying the crash in my head, feeling that impact all over again. It’s hard to even talk about it, so I just try to push it down, avoid thinking about it at all really.

What’s weird, though, is I can remember some parts of the accident so clearly, like the sound of the screeching tires, but then other parts, like how I actually got out of the car, are just a blur. It feels like my mind is just… blank sometimes. I used to be so outgoing, but now it’s like there’s a wall up. I don’t feel much joy in running the salon anymore, or really anything, it’s just a flat feeling. And my temper! I’ll snap at my stylists for the smallest thing, just a sudden burst of anger that comes out of nowhere. Even a light tap on my shoulder from a colleague can make me jump out of my skin – it’s embarrassing."
D018-D020_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

    C. Binge-Eating Disorder

D018-D020_h007.question:

D018-D020_h012.question:
